notes: Campaign B3 unit (gendn-g8o) for a legacy-unassessed v149 page. The page carried zero id attributes, so no selector could resolve to it. Six existing headings gained ids: context (at a glance), why-it-exists, error-contract (Error type contract, h3), syntax (Affected APIs, h3), examples (the first <pre><code> example's h3), and compatibility (browser support). The two h3 ids are necessary because fragmentAfterId() slices to the next <h1-3>: the 'shape of the change' and 'example' h2s each have an h3 immediately inside, so an id on those h2s would resolve to an empty fragment. No prose was reworded and no example block was added (the page already had two <pre><code> blocks). In-unit citation repair: the 'why it exists' span named two sources ('chromestatus' linked, 'blink-dev Intent to Ship thread' plain text); AGENTS.md:91 forbids one nearby link from covering another named source, so 'blink-dev Intent to Ship thread' was wrapped in its own link to the ChromeStatus intent_thread_url (curl 200, redirects to the groups.google.com thread). SOURCES RE-FETCHED, NOT ASSUMED (2026-10-07): the W3C payment-request #payment-handler-indicates-an-internal-error-algorithm fragment is live and its algorithm text is 'Let |error| be an OperationError DOMException... reject request.[[acceptPromise]] with |error|'; the ChromeStatus record 5942637229113344 summary matches the page's OperationError-vs-AbortError contract. CARRIED DISAGREEMENTS — BOTH SIDES STATED, NEITHER ADJUDICATED: (1) MDN PaymentRequest.show() still documents the OLD exception list (AbortError, InvalidStateError, NotSupportedError, SecurityError) and says 'The promise is also rejected with AbortError if the user cancels the payment request.' with no OperationError case, while this page documents the Chrome 149 change that show() now also rejects with OperationError for an internal payment app error. (2) The page's #compatibility table reads Firefox 'No signal (as of Chrome 149)' and Safari 'No signal (as of Chrome 149)', while the cited ChromeStatus record's ff view reads 'N/A' (notes: 'Firefox does not ship Payment Request or Payment Handler') and its safari view reads 'Positive'. (3) The page's #context reads 'Shipped in Chrome 149 / Edge 149' and 'Status: Enabled by default', while the cited ChromeStatus record's chrome status reads 'Proposed' (its ship stage still carries desktop_first/android_first/webview_first 149). No divergence is adjudicated or resolved here; the implementer owns the disclosure sentences and their pins in scripts/source-disagreement.test.mjs.
